screens.prompt: Learn how to describe a food and drink pairing.

before.text: チーズにワインがよく合います。

Noun に noun が合う describes a pairing: チーズにワインが合う, wine goes well with cheese. Adding は after に focuses or contrasts the pairing: チーズにはワインが合う. 合う（あう）means fit or go well with; 会う（あう）means meet a person.

screens.prompt: Learn the expression for personal taste.

before.text: この料理は私の口に合います。

Person の口に合う means to suit that person’s taste. お口 adds respect when asking a guest about their taste; do not elevate your own mouth this way. 口に合いませんでした frames a past dislike as personal taste. It can be softer than calling food bad, but tact still depends on the situation.

audio.text: この料理は私の口に合います。
audio.reading: この りょうりは わたしの くちに あいます。

screens.prompt: Listen. What is the host asking about?

options.text: Whether the guest likes the taste
Whether the guest has eaten here before

after.text: The host is asking about the guest’s personal taste. This feedback gives the question’s purpose without a full listening transcript.

audio.text: この料理はお口に合いますか。
audio.reading: この りょうりは おくちに あいますか。

feedbackCategories: Personal opinion idiom; no full transcript

screens.prompt: Listen and reconstruct the mouth word and two-character wondering ending.

after.text: あなたの口に合うかな。
after.secondary: あなたの くちに あうかな。

after.text: I wonder whether it will suit your taste.

Person の口に合う means to suit that person’s taste. お口 adds respect when asking a guest about their taste; do not elevate your own mouth this way. 口に合いませんでした frames a past dislike as personal taste. It can be softer than calling food bad, but tact still depends on the situation. Plain 合う takes casual wondering かな directly; the complete phrase is person の口に合う.

screens.prompt: Listen and build the host’s respectful tasting invitation.

after.text: Please try it and see whether it suits your taste.
お口 respectfully refers to the guest’s taste. 召し上がる is respectful eating/drinking; 召し上がってみてください invites the guest to try it. Use respectful forms for the guest’s action.

screens.prompt: Learn the noun for a scent or smell.

before.text: カレーの匂いがします。いい匂いですね。
It smells of curry. It smells good.
匂い（におい）is a scent or smell; it is also written におい. Noun + の匂い identifies what something smells of: カレーの匂い. いい匂い means a pleasant smell; the noun itself does not always mean a pleasant smell.

audio.text: カレーの匂いがします。いい匂いですね。
audio.reading: かれーの においが します。いい においですね。

screens.prompt: Read and listen. Is the statement true or false?
screens.statement: The speaker thinks the food’s smell is pleasant and it seems delicious.

before.text: いい匂いがしますね。おいしそうです。

after.text: いい匂い marks a pleasant smell. おいしそう expresses an impression that something seems delicious, not certainty about its taste.

audio.text: いい匂いがしますね。おいしそうです。
audio.reading: いい においが しますね。おいしそうです。

before.text: この魚は新鮮です。新鮮な魚を食べたいです。
This fish is fresh. I would like to eat fresh fish.
新鮮（しんせん）is a な-adjective: 新鮮な魚, fresh fish; 魚が新鮮です, the fish is fresh. It also describes things such as fresh air. It does not take an extra い ending.

screens.prompt: Listen and build the two reasons followed by the opinion.

after.text: この料理は、いい匂いがするし、味もいいし、おすすめです。

after.text: This dish smells good and tastes good, so I recommend it.
Plain predicates before し list reasons: 匂いがするし and 味もいいし. 匂い is the smell, 味（あじ）the taste. Either reason may come first.
